subject: Renewal proposal and ramp schedule for Avery Systems
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie@averysys.com>, Avery Systems Contracts <contracts@averysys.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal and ramp schedule for Avery Systems

Hi Sophie / Contracts team,

Thanks again for the chat yesterday. Attached is a proposal that tries to balance Avery's desire for capacity earlier in the term with Redwood's need for committed revenue predictability. High-level:

- Term: 24 months (with an opt-out at month 18 if usage stays below agreed thresholds)
- Commit style: "staggered pulse" — a frontloaded pulse (40% of year 1 commit delivered in Q1), then three quarterly pulses to hit annual committed units.
- Co-terming: we can co-term to Avery's FYQ1 (co-term trigger and calendar alignment in SOW section 2.3).
- Auto-renew: proposed, but with a 60-day opt-out window; we can remove auto-renew if legal requires.
- Price & credits: see attached pricing grid and SOW v3. We included a modest onboarding credit tied to a technical success milestone.

Attachments: Avery_SOW_v3.pdf, avy_capacity_pulse_schedule.xlsx, redwood-pricing-grid.csv

If this aligns directionally, I can route the SOW to Contracts and loop in Finance for an accelerated invoice if Avery wants to pre-pay the frontloaded pulse.

Next steps: let me know whether Avery prefers: (A) remove auto-renew, (B) keep auto-renew + 60-day opt-out, or (C) remove auto-renew but accept a slightly higher unit price.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for engineering teams
From: Sophie Lane <sophie@averysys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Avery Systems Contracts <contracts@averysys.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal and ramp schedule for Avery Systems

Jonas — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Co-terming: Yes, can you co-term to our FYQ1 (calendar Jan 1)? We want all vendor renewals to sync to that window.
2) Frontload: We have a product launch in Q1 and need more capacity earlier; can you move more of the frontloaded pulse into the first 60 days without changing total committed units?
3) Auto-renew: Legal prefers not to have auto-renew; they want an explicit renewal discussion 90 days before term end.
4) Pricing: We may be able to accept a small price bump in exchange for the frontload. Can you produce a revised SOW that aligns to the above and call out any impact to billing cadence?

Cc'ing Raj (procurement) to join once we have an updated SOW.

Best,
Sophie Lane
Director, Product Operations | Avery Systems
Sophie.Lane@averysys.com

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal and ramp schedule for Avery Systems — Sophie input

Team — Sophie pushed back on auto-renew and wants more frontload within the first 60 days. Also needs co-term to Jan 1. Can Finance/legal accept a 90-day renewal notice instead of auto-renew?

My asks:
- Lauren: can we model a 24-month term that co-terms to Jan 1 and includes an option to opt-out at month 18 (or a 90-day non-renew notice)? Also show the delta in ARR if we convert auto-renew -> manual renewal.
- Stephanie: if we move 10–15% more capacity into the first 60 days, what's the cash collection impact and can we offer a 4% onboarding credit as a concession?
- Neha: any constraints from capacity operations on frontloading more GPU-backed inference earlier? Is there a scheduling risk?

I think a clean play is to: 1) offer 24 months co-term to Jan 1; 2) frontload an additional ~15% of year 1 committed units into the first 60 days; 3) remove auto-renew and add 90-day explicit renewal notice; 4) offset with a small price increase or reduced onboarding credit.

I can own the customer convo if you can give me a final pricing matrix.

— Jonas
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal proposal and ramp schedule for Avery Systems — Sophie input

Jonas — Finance took a quick look and says the structure below is acceptable with approvals:

- Term: 24 months, co-term to 2027-01-01 (co-term effective date Jan 1, 2027).
- Commit: Staggered pulse with a frontloaded 55% of year-1 committed units delivered in the first 60 days (we can push the frontload up to 60% if Avery pays the first invoice up front).
- Auto-renew: removed; replaced with a mandatory renewal review 90 days before term end.
- Price/credits: unit price +3% if auto-renew is removed; alternate option: keep price flat and accept a 4% onboarding credit (applied as invoice credit after Q1 usage verification).
- Billing: We can do Net30 invoices for the standard flow; if Avery wants the larger frontload without pre-pay, we need milestone invoicing (two invoices: initial frontload invoice at signature, remainder on 90-day cadence).

Attachments: updated pricing grid (redwood-pricing-grid.csv) and an edited capacity schedule (avy_capacity_pulse_schedule.xlsx) showing the 55% frontload.

Stephanie — ops: can you confirm we have capacity headroom to honor a 55% frontload and what the risk looks like for the December/January ramp? If not, call out operational mitigations.

If this works, I'll have Legal prepare a one-page SOW amendment with the co-term language and renewal-notice clause.

-Lauren
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie@averysys.com>, Avery Systems Contracts <contracts@averysys.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@averysys.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Updated SOW and capacity cadence for Avery (attached)

Sophie / Contracts team —

Thanks for the input. Attached is a revised SOW (Avery_SOW_v3.pdf) and a capacity schedule that implements a 55% frontload in the first 60 days, co-term language to Jan 1, 2027, and the 90-day renewal notice in lieu of auto-renew. Key callouts:

- We added a clause that permits Avery to shift up to 10% of committed units across quarters in year 1 with 30 days' notice (to give some operational flexibility).
- Billing: initial invoice reflects the frontloaded 55% (Net30). Option to split the initial invoice into 2 milestones if Avery prefers (Finance will accept milestone invoicing).
- Pricing: two options are shown on page 2 of the pricing grid — (A) keep unit price flat + 4% onboarding credit OR (B) +3% unit price with no onboarding credit.

If you're comfortable with option A, we'll issue a DocuSign and route to Contracts for signature. If Avery wants to remove billing up-front entirely, we'll need a short note from Procurement confirming milestone schedule.

DocuSign link (draft): https://docusign.com/rdoc/3a7b8f
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/7421/AVY-5421

Would you like a quick 20-minute alignment call this afternoon to walk through the billing implications?

Best,
Jonas

Attachments: Avery_SOW_v3.pdf, avy_capacity_pulse_schedule.xlsx, redwood-pricing-grid.csv
From: Sophie Lane <sophie@averysys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@averysys.com>, Avery Systems Contracts <contracts@averysys.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Updated SOW and capacity cadence for Avery (attached)

Jonas — appreciate the fast turnaround. A few quick notes from Legal/Procurement:

1) We prefer option A (flat price + 4% onboarding credit).
2) Please remove the automatic milestone invoicing language and replace with a single initial invoice for the frontload (Net30) plus a clause allowing us to request a one-time split payment ONLY if we provide at least 10 business days' notice prior to signature.
3) Minor redline on co-term section: change "co-term effective date Jan 1, 2027" to "co-term effective date Jan 1, 2027 subject to Avery Systems' fiscal policy approval" — I'll have Contracts tighten that.

We'll sign once the SOW reflects the three items above. Raj is looped to finalize procurement language.

I'll expect an updated DocuSign by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sophie
Director, Product Operations
Avery Systems
